bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar to Set Up Teacher Training University, AI Ecosystem with Microsoft, Google, Sarvam AI
bihar_raw_news.content: Government Policies 1 min read Bihar to Set Up Teacher Training University, AI Ecosystem with Microsoft, Google, Sarvam AI: CM Samrat Choudhary He also said the state would develop a "modern AI ecosystem" in collaboration with Microsoft, Google, and Sarvam AI, under which teachers would be trained on the latest technologies in artificial intelligence. ETEducation Published On Sep 5, 2026 at 04:18 PM IST Select ETEducation as Preferred Choice on Google Copy Link Share on WhatsApp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bihar CM Choudhary said a "Teacher Training University" would be established for better training and capacity development of teachers Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary, in a Teachers' Day message posted on X, announced a set of education-sector resolutions by the state government, including a new teacher training university and a separate pay scale for honorarium-based teachers. Choudhary said a "Teacher Training University" would be established for better training and capacity development of teachers, and that a separate pay scale arrangement would be ensured for honorarium-based teachers. He also said the state would develop a "modern AI ecosystem" in collaboration with Microsoft, Google, and Sarvam AI, under which teachers would be trained on the latest technologies in artificial intelligence. Advt On higher education, Choudhary said efforts would be made to establish a center of Banaras Hindu University (BHU) in Bihar to expand access for the state's students. He added that payment of pending salaries for teachers of the Madrasa and Sanskrit boards had been initiated, so that teachers can receive their remuneration on time. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Mandates Pre-Approval for CBI Probes Involving State Officials - Devdiscourse
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Mandates Pre-Approval for CBI Probes Involving State Officials The Bihar government now requires the CBI to secure prior permission to investigate state officers, as per a recent notification. This development marks a significant shift, demanding individual approval for each case involving the state's apparatus, while aligning with the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946. Devdiscourse News Desk | Updated: 05-09-2026 13:05 IST | Created: 05-09-2026 13:05 IST Representative Image (File Photo/ANI). Image Credit: ANI Country: India SHARE Key Takeaways AI Summary Analyzing article... In a notable policy shift, the Bihar government has declared that the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) must obtain prior consent before conducting any investigations involving its state officers or employees. This directive, as per the Home Department's notification, was issued in the Governor of Bihar's name and hinges on Section 6 of the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946. The notification elaborates on the circumstances under which CBI's investigatory consent is granted generally, such as offences involving Central Government employees, Public Sector Undertakings, and specific private individuals. Yet, it stipulates that when Bihar's public servants or state-controlled entities are implicated, the state's explicit consent is mandatory. This stipulation ensures localized oversight, with the state evaluating investigatory permissions on a case-by-case basis, upon receipt of a proposal from the Delhi Special Police Establishment. Historically, the CBI's authority originated from the Special Police Establishment formed in 1941, tasked with probing wartime bribe and corruption charges in India. The crucial Delhi Special Police Establishment Act of 1946 empowered the CBI to investigate central corruption cases, a mandate now navigated with additional procedural layers in Bihar. bihar_raw_news.title: RVNL Wins ₹903 Cr Order from SJVN for Buxar Thermal Siding - PSU Connect
bihar_raw_news.content: New Delhi: Rail Vikas Nigam Limited has secured a major infrastructure order linked to one of SJVN’s key thermal projects. The company has received a Letter of Award from SJVN Thermal Private Limited (a wholly owned subsidiary of SJVN Limited) for the construction of a permanent railway siding along with an aerial track connection from the plant boundary to Chausa and Pawani Kamarpur at Buxar in Bihar. The work forms Phase-III of the infrastructure support for the 1,320 MW Buxar Thermal Power Project (BTPP). national_raw_news.title: 50 mins ago | National 42 President Droupadi Murmu pays tributes to teachers on occasion of Teachers’ Day
national_raw_news.content: President Droupadi Murmu today paid tributes to teachers across the country on the occasion of Teachers’ Day. Writing an article in an English daily, President Murmu described teaching as a noble responsibility that goes beyond imparting academic knowledge and plays a vital role in shaping individuals and the nation. She expressed gratitude to teachers for instilling knowledge, skills, values and motivation in the lives of crores of students. Recalling the legacy of former President Dr Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan, she noted that despite his achievements as a scholar, author and statesman, he regarded being a teacher as his most important role. She also recalled former President Dr A P J Abdul Kalam’s desire to be remembered as a teacher. Emphasising the enduring importance of the teacher-student relationship, President Murmu referred to the ancient ideal of ‘Acharyadevo Bhava’ and said teachers must treat students with love, patience and fairness while keeping their well-being foremost. She shared her own experiences of being guided by affectionate and dedicated teachers, saying their encouragement helped awaken confidence, courage and limitless potential within her. The President stressed that teachers do far more than teach a curriculum. Through their conduct and example, they mentor and inspire students, helping them develop the ability to think independently, ask questions, exercise judgement and face challenges with confidence. She added that such education is essential for nurturing future entrepreneurs, scientists, artists and citizens capable of finding innovative solutions to emerging challenges. Calling teaching ‘the sacred task of shaping humanity’, President Murmu also recalled her own experience as a teacher at the Sri Aurobindo Integral School in Rairangpur, Odisha. She remembered participating in students’ musical performances, sports and plays, and taking them on outings where they could learn about nature and the environment. The President said she continues to cherish her bond with many of her former students and has also learnt from their spontaneity and curiosity. She also highlighted her continued engagement with children, including teaching students at a school on the premises around Rashtrapati Bhavan about environmental conservation. She also recalled establishing a residential school in her village around eleven years ago for children from disadvantaged families and those who had lost their parents. She said seeing the children thrive gives her a deep sense of fulfilment. President Murmu further emphasised that the responsibility of educating children does not rest with teachers alone. Parents, guardians and society also have an important role to play, while individuals who become role models through their conduct and achievements can serve as valuable sources of inspiration for children. She said teachers have a sacred responsibility to uphold the trust placed in them by parents and guardians and stressed that their behaviour should nurture confidence rather than create fear, anxiety or a sense of inferiority among children. She underlined that a good teacher helps students become the best versions of themselves and guides them towards becoming good human beings. Looking ahead, President Murmu called upon teachers to help shape generations that value India’s cultural heritage and traditions, develop a scientific outlook, work for the welfare of humanity, uphold the ideal of Antyodaya, protect the environment and living creatures, pursue excellence and move forward with the spirit of ‘Nation First’. She also appealed to every citizen to hold committed and sincere teachers in the highest esteem. She expressed confidence that with the contribution of dedicated teachers, India will continue to learn, progress and ultimately lead.

national_raw_news.title: 1 hour ago | International 176 UN votes to adopt new world map reflecting accurate size of Africa
national_raw_news.content: The UN General Assembly has voted to replace the traditional world map with one that more accurately reflects the size of Africa. The “Correct the Map” resolution, sponsored by Togo and backed by African Union (AU) members, passed with the support of 164 nations, including India, France and the UK. The United States was the only nation to vote against it, while six countries abstained. The UN vote is non-binding, but it will encourage governments and institutions to stop using the traditional Mercator map. The Mercator map, which has been in common use since the 16th Century, has come under criticism as it shows Africa as similar in size to Greenland, even though it is 14 times larger. Critics say this leads to the development needs and potential for countries near the equator to be minimised. The Mercator map was designed in 1569 by the Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator to help European explorers navigate across the world. The map makes countries near the poles appear much larger than they really are. The distortion of his map is a result of the fact that it is impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart. In an effort to correct this, a team of cartographers in 2018 created an equal area map they called the Equal Earth projection, which shows the relative sizes of continents more accurately. In February, the African Union’s 54 member states adopted it and said it more accurately represents the sizes of all continents, particularly Africa. Ahead of the voting, Togolese Foreign Minister Robert Dussey, talking to media, said a fair world begins with a fair map. At a UN briefing, Mr Dussey said, a map is never neutral. It shapes perceptions and influences how the place of peoples and continents in the world is understood. France has also backed the change and said it plans to stop using the Mercator map. However, the United States criticised the UN vote, arguing that the General Assembly should focus on more serious global issues. Campaigners say maps are more than just guides for travellers, they shape how regions are perceived politically and economically.

national_raw_news.title: Government systems should remain responsive to employees, families: Minister
national_raw_news.content: Government systems should remain responsive to employees, families: Minister | MorungExpress | morungexpress.com Government systems should remain responsive to employees, families: Minister Government systems should remain responsive to employees, families: Minister (Photo: PIB) India 5th September 2026 New Delhi, September 5 (IANS): Union Minister Dr Jitendra Singh called for continued efforts to make government service rules more responsive to the needs of employees and their families, an official statement said on Saturday. Speaking at the launch of the ‘CSS Shield’ initiative of the Central Secretariat Service (CSS) Forum, the minister said collective efforts to support bereaved families could create a new culture of standing by colleagues in times of sudden loss. The initiative is a mutual support mechanism for the bereaved families of CSS officers. He presented financial assistance to the families of two deceased officers -- Mohan Chandra Bhatt and Rajendra Chandra -- as part of the initiative. “The mechanism is not difficult to implement, what matters is the collective will and willingness to contribute,” according to the minister. He said that when colleagues come together as one family to support a bereaved family, it sends a meaningful message beyond the organisation itself and added that the initiative was in keeping with the larger effort of the government to make service systems more responsive to the needs of employees and their families. Referring to the approach of the government under Prime Minister Narendra Modi, the minister said there was continuous encouragement to review rules and procedures and make necessary changes wherever existing arrangements could be improved. In addition, representatives of the CSS Forum said the forum had been supporting the families of deceased CSS officers through voluntary contributions even before the formal launch of CSS Shield, according to the government. The experience during the COVID-19 period when a number of CSS officers lost their lives further strengthened the need for a structured mechanism of mutual support, according to the government. The forum said that since 2020, CSS officers had collectively contributed around Rs 1.30 crore towards financial assistance for the families of approximately 65-70 deceased officers. Under the new initiative, the forum seeks to provide at least Rs 15 lakh to a bereaved family, while its larger objective is to progressively enhance the assistance as participation increases, the government said.
